anchors.text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.
For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

anchors.text: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?
The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
Delight thyself also in the LORD: and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.
For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.
The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?
Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy.
Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.

books.name: Proverbs
gists: Wisdom calls for heed; rejecting it leads to ruin and fear.
Seek wisdom to gain understanding, protection, and deliverance from evil.
Trust the Lord; embrace His wisdom for true life and peace.
A father encourages children to pursue wisdom and avoid evil.
Avoid temptations to preserve honor and fidelity for lasting satisfaction.
Avoid surety, learn diligence, and heed parental commands against pitfalls.
A father warns his son against seduction and the dangers of adultery.
Wisdom invites all to pursue understanding and offers life and favor.
Wisdom invites the simple, while folly leads to death; fear of the LORD is essential.
Wisdom brings joy and prosperity, while folly leads to sorrow and poverty.
Integrity brings safety and blessing; wickedness leads to ruin.
Loving instruction brings knowledge; the wicked face ruin and shame.
Wisdom brings instruction, diligence yields abundance, and righteousness ensures protection.
Wisdom nurtures; folly ruins; the fear of the LORD brings life.
Soft answers calm anger; the LORD values wisdom and righteousness.
God guides plans; humility and righteousness yield wisdom and favor.
Better to have peace with little than much with strife.
Wisdom and humility bring honor; words have powerful consequences in life.
Integrity prevails over folly; wisdom and discipline lead to life.
Wine deceives; diligence and integrity are essential for a good life.
The LORD directs hearts, values justice, and rewards wisdom over wickedness.
A good name is valuable; train children wisely and avoid debt.
Avoid greed, seek wisdom, and shun excess and bad company.
Pursue wisdom, avoid envy, and work diligently in all endeavors.
Hezekiah preserves Solomon's proverbs on wisdom, humility, and conflict resolution.
Folly and sloth lead to shame, strife, and ruin.
Value friendship and wisdom; avoid boasting and embrace rebuke.
The wicked fear, the righteous stand firm, and wise leadership blesses a land.
Stubbornness leads to ruin; righteousness brings joy; pride causes strife.
Agur expresses humility, reveres God, and observes creation's wisdom.
A mother advises wisdom, justice, and praises a virtuous woman.

anchors.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.
A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.

books.name: Ecclesiastes
gists: All is vanity; nothing is new, and wisdom brings sorrow.
The pursuit of pleasure and wisdom reveals life's futility; joy is God's gift.
Everything has a time; joy in labor is a divine gift.
Oppression leads to suffering, but companionship and wisdom offer strength.
Approach God reverently; enjoy the fruits of honest labor.
Riches and long life offer no true joy or contentment.
Wisdom's value, reflection on life, and the balance of joy and sorrow.
Wisdom leads to boldness; life's injustices cause existential reflection.
Death equally affects all; embrace life and cherish wisdom despite uncertainty.
Folly undermines wisdom; wise conduct guides better than foolishness.
Be generous, work hard, enjoy youth, and remember life's brevity.
Remember your Creator before old age and the inevitable return to God.

anchors.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

books.name: Song of Solomon
gists: The speaker expresses longing and admiration for her beloved's beauty.

The speaker seeks her beloved at night and brings him home.
The beloved praises his love's beauty and invites her to delight.
The beloved longs for her lover and searches for him.
The Shulamite praises her beloved's beauty and expresses their mutual love.
The lovers admire each other amidst nature's beauty and mutual desire.
The speaker expresses love's strength, offers caution, and recalls cherished memories.

anchors.text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
